title: Put the right plugs of two devices in their holders when the cables run hidden under a cover
instruction: Put the plug of the red box's cable in the red holder and the plug of the blue box's cable in the blue holder. Leave the other plugs where they are.
context: When cables run hidden under a cover, a desk tray or a floor duct, which loose plug belongs to which device cannot be seen. Here five identical cables cross out of sight and every plug lies away from its own device, so looking does not answer the question: the robot has to tug a cable where it leaves its device and see which plug moves. Taking the wrong plug is the failure that matters, because it disconnects or moves the wrong device.
setup: Station table, positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases projected onto the table (x forward away from the robot, y to the robot's left). Devices: five 9 x 9 x 7 cm boxes (3D-printed PLA or painted wooden blocks) fixed to the table, robot-facing side at x 53, centred at y +24 (yellow), +12 (red), 0 (green), -12 (blue) and -24 (orange). Cover: a grey 15 x 86 x 1 cm plate (PLA or plywood) spanning x 25 to 40 and y -43 to +43, its underside 2.5 cm above the table, on two 1 cm thick end walls at y +42.5 and -42.5, fixed to the table. Under the cover, hidden: ten smooth grey guide posts (PTFE), 4 cm diameter and 8 mm tall, fixed to the table, five at x 37.5 (y +21.3, +9.3, +2.7, -9.3, -21.3) and five at x 27.5 (y +27.3, +13.3, +4.7, -14.7, -25.3). Cables: five identical black 8 mm round PVC cords, each fixed (glued, with strain relief) into the robot-facing side of its box 1.3 cm above the table, each ending in an identical black 3D-printed PLA plug, 35 x 16 x 12 mm (long side along the cable), 15 g. Lengths: yellow 49.3, red 67.0, green 43.6, blue 69.0, orange 40.0 cm. Each cable comes down to the table within 5 cm (the yellow, red and orange ones leave their box turned 17, 9 and 6 degrees to the robot's right and straighten within 2 cm) and runs straight towards the robot along its box's centre line to the far row of posts, bends round one of them, runs diagonally under the cover, bends round a post of the near row and comes out of the cover straight towards the robot, its plug lying flat with its centre at x 17. The routes, by box: yellow from y +24 round posts (37.5, +21.3) and (27.5, +4.7) to its plug at y +2; red from y +12 round (37.5, +9.3) and (27.5, -25.3) to y -28; green from y 0 round (37.5, +2.7) and (27.5, +13.3) to y +16; blue from y -12 round (37.5, -9.3) and (27.5, +27.3) to y +30; orange from y -24 round (37.5, -21.3) and (27.5, -14.7) to y -12. Every bend wraps its post at 2.7 cm from the post's centre. Where two diagonals cross, the later one in the laying order blue, red, yellow, green, orange lies on top (red over blue, yellow over blue, green over yellow, red and blue, orange over red). Plug holders: two U-channels (3D-printed PLA) fixed to the table on either side of the midline, each with two side walls 45 mm long (along x), 4 mm thick and 8 mm tall, 40 mm apart (inner slot 45 x 40 mm, the table is its floor), closed on the robot side by a white end stop 4 mm thick, 48 mm wide and 20 mm tall, open at the far end. The holder with blue side walls has its slot centre at x 11, y +18; the holder with red side walls at x 11, y -18.
scoring: Score 0 if at any moment the yellow, green or orange box's plug is more than 5 cm (3D) from where it lay at the start, whether picked up, pushed or slid by a tug on its cable (tape marks; judged from the top-camera video), or the red box's plug lies in the blue holder or the blue box's plug in the red holder; also 0 if a cable is pulled out of its box (its end at the box moves more than 1 cm). Boxes, cover, posts and holders are fixed to the table. A plug lies in a holder when it is between the holder's side walls, lying on the table, inside the slot or sticking out of its open far end by at most 1 cm. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 if the red box's plug lies in the red holder and the blue box's plug in the blue holder, each released (no gripper within 3 cm of its centre); 0.5 if exactly one of the two lies released in its own holder; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing. Success (1.0) once the full condition has held for 1 s with both plugs at rest.
reset_notes: Lay the cables in the order blue, red, yellow, green, orange: each straight from its box along its box's centre line, round its far post, diagonally to its near post, round it and straight out to its plug mark at x 17, pulled snug against both posts. Plugs flat, long side along the cable. Remove anything from the holders.
fidelity: Each cable is a chain of 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs (no twist, no plasticity); plugs are rigid boxes; box ends are fixed. Boxes, cover, posts and holders are fixed rigid shapes; holders have no latch. Real cords kink less sharply at the posts and can twist. A real taut cable would stop the plug short of its holder; the simulated arm can pull harder, so each box fixing lets go above 300 N and a pulled-out cable scores 0 (same outcome).
